summary: kepler pulls sole dependency from non-registry host with install script enabled
details: The kepler package ships a trivial stub index.js that only exports a name/version constant. Its package.json and npm-shrinkwrap.json pin its single dependency, `flag-serial-object-syntax`, to a tarball URL at `https://artifacts.yosiroute.com/npm/flag-serial-object-syntax` — a third-party host, not the npm registry. The shrinkwrap entry for that dependency has `hasInstallScript: true`, so `npm install kepler` downloads the tarball from artifacts.yosiroute.com and runs its lifecycle scripts on the installing machine. Because the package's own code is a stub with no functionality, the sole effect of installing kepler is to fetch and execute install-time code hosted at a publisher-chosen, non-registry endpoint. The delivered bytes are mutable at the host and are not pinned by hash or signature.

cwes.description: The product contains code that appears to be malicious in nature.
cwes.name: Embedded Malicious Code
